section: Unemployment - types (structural, frictional, cyclical, disguised, seasonal, educated)
subsections: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

accepted.s: A person who is able and willing to work but does not get any job is experiencing which type of unemployment?
accepted.x: Open unemployment exists when a person is willing and able to work but has no job at all.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the direct definition from closely related classifications.
accepted.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes hidden or disguised unemployment?
o: Workers are temporarily dismissed during a recession
Workers refuse jobs because the prevailing wage is low
Persons appear to be employed but make no effective contribution to output
Workers change jobs while searching for a better match
accepted.x: In hidden or disguised unemployment, persons appear to be employed, but their removal does not reduce output because they contribute nothing or very little to production.
accepted.tq: Separate apparent employment from actual productive contribution.
accepted.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding voluntary and involuntary unemployment:
1. Voluntary unemployment occurs when a person is unwilling to work at the prevailing wage.
2. Involuntary unemployment occurs when a person is willing to work at the prevailing wage but cannot find a job.
3. The labour force counts only voluntary unemployment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The labour force counts involuntary unemployment, not only voluntary unemployment.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses the voluntary–involuntary distinction.
accepted.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

accepted.s:
Which of the following may lead to voluntary unemployment?
1. High benefits that reduce the incentive to accept work
2. A high marginal tax rate
3. Waiting for a better-suited job
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: High benefits, a high marginal tax rate and waiting for a better-suited job are all stated causes of voluntary unemployment.
accepted.tq: Use the all-inclusive option when each listed cause belongs to the same category.
accepted.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

accepted.s: Unemployment that persists over a long period is generally classified as:
accepted.x: Chronic unemployment is long-term unemployment that persists over an extended period.
accepted.tq: Match the duration-based description with the exact term.
accepted.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Unemployment trap — unemployment caused by seasonal agricultural activity
Casual unemployment — unemployment lasting for more than twelve months
Long-term unemployment — unemployment arising only from a temporary recession
Classical unemployment — unemployment caused by wages being too high
accepted.x: Classical, or real-wage, unemployment occurs when wages are too high. Long-term unemployment refers to unemployment exceeding twelve months, while casual unemployment involves day-to-day contract work and an unemployment trap may arise when benefits discourage work.
accepted.tq: Check the exact cause attached to each similar unemployment term.
accepted.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

accepted.s: A worker employed on a day-to-day contract basis is most appropriately associated with:
accepted.x: Casual employment is based on day-to-day contract work; the classification is distinct from chronic and classical unemployment.
accepted.tq: Apply the employment arrangement rather than the duration or wage condition.
accepted.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

accepted.s: A person who has remained unemployed for more than 12 months falls under which category?
accepted.x: Long-term unemployment is defined here as unemployment lasting for more than twelve months.
accepted.tq: Use the stated time threshold to identify the classification.
accepted.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

accepted.s: Which situation illustrates an unemployment trap?
o: Benefits discourage a person from accepting available work
Automation replaces a routine manufacturing task
A worker changes jobs while searching for a better match
A recession reduces aggregate demand for labour
accepted.x: An unemployment trap occurs when benefits reduce the incentive to work and discourage acceptance of available employment.
accepted.tq: Identify the classification from its behavioural mechanism.
accepted.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

accepted.s:
With reference to full employment, consider the following statements:
1. Every person willing to work at the prevailing wage finds work.
2. Full employment implies that frictional unemployment cannot exist.
3. Structural unemployment may still exist at full employment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Full employment means that everyone willing to work at the prevailing wage finds work, but frictional and structural unemployment may still exist.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute claim that full employment eliminates every form of unemployment.
accepted.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

accepted.s: The natural rate of unemployment is composed of:
accepted.x: The natural rate is the combination of frictional and structural unemployment existing at full employment.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact components of a standard composite concept.
accepted.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

accepted.s: The concept of the natural rate of unemployment is particularly associated with:
accepted.x: The concept of the natural rate of unemployment is associated with Milton Friedman.
accepted.tq: Link the named economist with the specific concept rather than a related curve or law.
accepted.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

accepted.s: Technological unemployment is best understood as:
o: Job loss caused exclusively by a fall in aggregate demand
Unemployment caused by a worker voluntarily rejecting the prevailing wage
Temporary unemployment during the agricultural off-season
Job loss caused by changes in technology and treated as a subtype of structural unemployment
accepted.x: Technological unemployment results from technological change and is a subtype of structural unemployment.
accepted.tq: Use the cause-and-classification link to distinguish technological from cyclical unemployment.

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the likely labour-market effect of automation and artificial intelligence?
1. Automation in manufacturing may reduce demand for low-skilled and routine jobs.
2. Artificial intelligence in services may reduce demand for routine jobs.
3. Technological change can generate structural unemployment.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Automation in manufacturing and AI in services can reduce demand for low-skilled and routine jobs, and the resulting technological unemployment is structural in character.
accepted.tq: Combine the sector-specific examples with their common structural effect.

accepted.s: Jobless growth is more likely when economic growth is driven mainly by:
o: Labour-intensive manufacturing rather than capital-intensive activities
Capital-intensive sectors such as information technology and finance rather than labour-intensive manufacturing
accepted.x: Growth led by capital-intensive sectors such as IT and finance, instead of labour-intensive manufacturing, can produce jobless growth.
accepted.tq: Focus on the reversed capital-intensive versus labour-intensive comparison.

accepted.s: The Phillips curve was named after A.W. Phillips, whose relevant work dates to:
accepted.x: The Phillips curve is named after A.W. Phillips and is associated with his 1958 work.
accepted.tq: Use the date-specific option rather than confusing it with later developments of the theory.

accepted.s: The traditional trade-off between inflation and unemployment breaks down in a situation of:
o: Stable prices with potential output growth
Stagflation, characterised by high inflation and high unemployment
accepted.x: Stagflation combines high inflation with high unemployment and therefore breaks down the traditional Phillips-curve trade-off.
accepted.tq: Identify the unusual combination that contradicts the traditional inverse relationship.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the long-run Phillips curve:
1. It is vertical at the natural rate of unemployment.
2. The long-run formulation is associated with Friedman and Phelps.
3. It establishes a permanent trade-off between inflation and unemployment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The long-run Phillips curve is vertical at the natural rate and is associated with Friedman and Phelps. It does not establish a permanent trade-off between inflation and unemployment.
accepted.tq: Separate the short-run trade-off from the long-run vertical-curve proposition.

accepted.s: According to Okun's law, a one percentage point rise in unemployment above the natural rate is associated approximately with:
o: A 2% rise in output above potential GDP
A 1% rise in output above potential GDP
A 2% fall in output below potential GDP
A 5% fall in output below potential GDP
accepted.x: Okun's law states that a one percentage point increase in unemployment above the natural rate is associated with roughly a 2% reduction in output below potential GDP.
accepted.tq: Track both parts of the quantitative relationship: the unemployment point and the output percentage.

accepted.s: Okun's law is associated with:
accepted.x: The inverse relationship between unemployment and the gap between actual and potential output is known as Okun's law, associated with Arthur Okun.
accepted.tq: Match the economic law with its principal economist.

accepted.s: According to the monthly PLFS data cited for May 2026, India's unemployment rate was:
accepted.x: The monthly PLFS unemployment rate rose to 5.5% in May 2026 from 5.2% in April 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the current-month value from the immediately preceding month and other comparative figures.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly presents the monthly PLFS unemployment-rate movement cited for India?
o: It rose from 3.2% in April 2026 to 4.1% in May 2026.
It declined from 5.5% in April 2026 to 5.2% in May 2026.
It remained unchanged at 5.2% during April and May 2026.
It rose from 5.2% in April 2026 to 5.5% in May 2026.
accepted.x: The unemployment rate increased from 5.2% in April 2026 to 5.5% in May 2026.
accepted.tq: Check the direction of change as well as the two month-specific figures.

accepted.s: For May 2026, the rural and urban unemployment rates cited for India were respectively:
accepted.x: The cited May 2026 rates were 5.1% for rural areas and 6.4% for urban areas.
accepted.tq: Preserve the order of the paired rural and urban figures.

accepted.s: Which statement regarding seasonal labour migration is correct?
o: Nearly 30–35 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
Nearly 3–5 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
More than 100 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
Nearly 10–15 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
accepted.x: Approximately 30–35 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated range rather than selecting a nearby but incorrect magnitude.

accepted.s: The unemployment rate in Andhra Pradesh, compared with the all-India rate cited for the PLFS 2023–24 and APSES 2024–25 comparison, was:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded 4.1% unemployment compared with 3.2% for India, making the AP rate higher by 0.9 percentage points.
accepted.tq: Subtract the paired rates and retain the direction of the comparison.

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly states the unemployment indicators for Andhra Pradesh cited in the comparison?
1. Overall unemployment rate in Andhra Pradesh was 4.1%.
2. Youth unemployment rate for the 15–29 age group was 17.5%.
3. Urban female youth unemployment was 29.1%.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three figures are correct: overall unemployment was 4.1%, youth unemployment for ages 15–29 was 17.5%, and urban female youth unemployment was 29.1%.
accepted.tq: Use the all-inclusive option after verifying each age- and gender-specific figure.

accepted.s: In the overall gender-wise unemployment figures cited for Andhra Pradesh, which comparison is correct?
o: Female and male unemployment were both 4.1%.
Female unemployment was 29.1% and male unemployment was 17.5%.
Female unemployment was 3.7% and male unemployment was 4.3%.
Female unemployment was 4.3% and male unemployment was 3.7%.
accepted.x: The cited overall figures were 3.7% for females and 4.3% for males.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the two gender-specific values.

accepted.s: A decline in the measured unemployment rate may fail to indicate genuine job creation when it results from:
o: A rise in potential GDP caused by technology
A permanent reduction in the labour force due to higher wages
accepted.x: A falling unemployment rate may reflect people entering low-productivity work under distress rather than the creation of good or adequate jobs.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an apparently favourable indicator from its possible underlying labour-market condition.

accepted.s: Which of the following comparisons between India and developed countries is correct?
o: India mainly faces cyclical unemployment, whereas developed countries mainly face disguised unemployment.
Developed countries mainly face seasonal unemployment, whereas India mainly faces classical unemployment.
India mainly faces structural and disguised unemployment, whereas developed countries mainly face cyclical, demand-deficient unemployment.
Both India and developed countries mainly face only frictional unemployment.
accepted.x: India's unemployment is characterised as structural and disguised, while developed countries are described as facing mainly cyclical or demand-deficient unemployment.
accepted.tq: Keep both sides of the comparative classification aligned with the stated economic context.

accepted.s: Which economist is associated with the explanation of cyclical unemployment in developed countries as demand-deficient unemployment?
accepted.x: The demand-deficiency explanation of cyclical unemployment is associated with Keynes.
accepted.tq: Match the explanatory framework with the economist associated with it.
